title: The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower

scenes.say: In 1925, a con man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back and tried to sell it again.
His name was Victor Lustig. Charming, well dressed, and one of the smoothest con artists in history.
In Paris, he read a newspaper story about how expensive the tower had become to repair. That gave him an idea.
scenes.head: THE TOWER|COSTS A|FORTUNE

scenes.say: Posing as a government official, he invited six scrap metal dealers to a secret meeting at a luxury hotel.
He told them the city was tearing the tower down and selling it for scrap. And they must tell no one.
One dealer, Andre Poisson, took the bait. Lustig even hinted he wanted a bribe, which made him seem like a real, corrupt official.
Lustig took the money and fled the country. Poisson was so embarrassed, he never told the police.
So Lustig came back to Paris and tried the very same trick again. This time, his target went to the police. And Lustig escaped again.
scenes.sub: the same trick, a second time

scenes.say: Here is the lesson. Lustig's tricks still work today. An official sounding stranger. A secret deal. And pressure to act fast.
So if anyone asks you to keep a deal secret and decide fast, slow down. That is exactly how scams work.
Follow Odd Archive for more history with a lesson.
